speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing episodes of dizziness and vertigo; to help me identify the cause, have you noticed if these spells are triggered by changes in your head position, such as rolling over in bed or looking up?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old woman. The patient presents with sudden episodes of dizziness that are position dependent. She describes experiencing a false sensation of motion and occasional spinning, indicative of vertigo. She denies any recent illnesses, injuries, or significant changes in health status, apart from age-related hearing loss (presbycusis).

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is excellent; the fact that the dizziness is triggered by head movements strongly suggests a benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV). To confirm this, I need to know if you have experienced any new hearing loss, ringing in your ears (tinnitus), or sudden deafness in either ear during these spells.

Also, on a scale of one to ten, how severe is the spinning sensation during an episode?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodes of dizziness and spinning sensation. I also have Position dependent vertigo, No recent illness, No hearing loss besides presbycusis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV).

Given your age, the clear positional trigger, and the absence of hearing loss or other neurological deficits, I am confident in this diagnosis. Would you like me to proceed with the Dix-Hallpike maneuver to confirm the diagnosis and identify the affected canal?
